note: Vulcan County campground below the Twin Valley Dam on the Little Bow River (Twin Valley Reservoir), ~15 min east of Hwy 2 via Hwy 529: one large oval loop of drive-in sites, with a boat dock, day-use picnic area and walking trails. --Claude
summary: Campground's own site (twinvalleycampground.ca) found and read: C$20 non-powered / C$25 powered (fees were empty), FCFS weekdays and regular weekends with phone reservations for long weekends and groups, outhouses. Riverfront looks overstated (riverview recommended); phone and website changes suggested.
flags: WEBSITE/PHONE: the campground has its own site https://www.twinvalleycampground.ca/ (200; Google links a Facebook page). Reservations phone on that site 403-485-3700; Google Maps 'Twin Valley Campground' 4.4 from 29 reviews, phone 403-485-3606. Stored 403-485-2241 (Vulcan County office) and the stored county/tourism URLs show no campground page (vulcancounty.ab.ca search finds only a blue-green algae advisory for the reservoir; explorevulcancounty.com rendered nothing to curl - UNREAD). Suggest website https://www.twinvalleycampground.ca/ and phone 403-485-3700.

OWNERSHIP: the operator site does not name the operator and the County site no longer has a campground page, so whether Vulcan County still runs it (stored local) or a contractor/private operator does is unconfirmed; left local. The site also advertises 'Seasonal Camping' (date TBD).

WATERFRONT (stored riverfront - recommend riverview): on Esri imagery the westernmost RV pads of the oval are about 80 m from the Little Bow River's east bank (stored evidence said ~48-50 m), and the campground's own outer loop road plus a trail run between the pads and the river; the river is about 28-33 m wide. Over 50 m and behind the loop road, so riverfront is not met; recommend riverview.
PRICE: C$20-25 a night, no gate issue (local). Season not stated anywhere I read; none stored.
PIN (50.22774,-113.40164): centre of the campground oval; Google's 50.22761,-113.40109 is about 40 m away. No move.
